headline: Advancements in Quantum Complexity, States, and Metrology
summary: Today's research spans fundamental quantum theory and metrology, highlighting new complexity class collapses, state tomography tools, and Rydberg atom calibration. Together, these papers push forward our theoretical understanding of quantum circuits and our practical capabilities in measurement.

themes.title: Quantum Complexity and Circuit Limits
themes.body: New insights into quantum complexity reveal collapses in verification classes such as PureSuperQMA, while Fourier hierarchy studies prove that additional Hadamard layers strictly increase computational power.

themes.title: Quantum States and Simulation Cost
themes.body: Researchers constructed positive partial transpose states with near-maximal Schmidt numbers and analyzed the resource costs of simulating classically tractable quantum circuits versus running them on real hardware.

themes.title: Tomography and Metrology
themes.body: Advances in practical quantum observation include an open-source Python package for high-fidelity quantum state tomography and a method for SI-traceable calibration of terahertz fields using Rydberg atoms.

connections.body: Both papers deal with structural properties and resource bounds of multipartite quantum states, focusing on Schmidt numbers in PPT states and density matrix reconstruction via tomography.
